facts.fact: Emilia Hare 是 The Jolly Boaters 酒馆后厅吧台的女工，几乎白天黑夜都在店里干活
facts.anchor: the young lady who worked most days and nights behind the public bar at The Jolly Boaters

facts.fact: 她恨母亲，因为到这家又吵又臭的店打工本来就是母亲的主意
facts.anchor: She hated her mother (whose idea it had been that she take a job in that noisy and malodorous establishment in the first place)

facts.fact: 她恨父亲，因为他一向什么都不说，只是照例顺从发号施令的妻子
facts.anchor: she hated her father (who had said nothing but only acquiesced, as ever, to his commanding wife)

facts.fact: 她恨自己的雇主——那个叫 Bill Crickmore 的满口脏话的男人，常偷喝自家酒窖的酒
facts.anchor: She hated her employer (that foul-mouthed gentleman called Bill Crickmore who resorted too often to the contents of his own cellar)

facts.fact: 她在人前永远挂着刀枪不入的轻蔑神色，可这神色反倒招来更多追求者，令她恼火
facts.anchor: She wore at all times in public a look of imperishable scorn which, to her infuriation, seemed to serve only to attract admirers to a greater degree

facts.fact: 唯一让她露出真笑的那个人在中午刚过一点点时走进吧台，跌跌撞撞朝她走来
facts.anchor: it was this gentleman who walked into the public bar at a little after noon and stumbled towards her

facts.fact: 那人走起路来脚下打晃，衣衫褴褛蓬乱，像前一晚几乎没睡
facts.anchor: He seemed to be swaying on his feet as he moved. He looked ragged, unkempt, as though he had barely slept (or not slept at all) the preceding night

facts.fact: Beck 说他打开了一扇再也关不上的门
facts.anchor: “I think that I have opened a door which I may not be able to close again.”

facts.fact: 他说脑子里那个声音属于一个叫 Marley 的死人
facts.anchor: A man, a dead man, called Marley.

facts.fact: 这位伦敦最负盛名的年轻灵媒抓过酒杯，把那团又黑又旋的液体一饮而尽
facts.anchor: The most celebrated young psychic medium in London seized the glass gratefully and drank deep of the dark and swirling liquid.

facts.fact: 就连盐也挡不住 Marley 多久
facts.anchor: Even the salt didn’t keep him out for long.

facts.fact: Beck 说想讲却收住，理由是这样不对、这样不公平
facts.anchor: “But it wouldn’t be right. It wouldn’t be fair.”

facts.fact: 她从地窖回来时，吧台空了，Beck 已经走了
facts.anchor: it was to find the bar empty and Mr Beck gone.

facts.fact: 面对空椅子她生出焦虑的悲伤，仿佛知道 Beck 即将犯下那桩可怕的事
facts.anchor: she felt an anxious sadness, as though she somehow knew the dreadful act which he was about to commit.
